lines: That remark had all the strength of loose gravel.
I have swept up gravel with firmer opinions than that.
If that thought were mortar, the wall would already be down.
I have seen broken stonework with better instincts than you.
You have the wit of wet gravel.
I have seen cracked cobble hold together better.
That idea lacks foundation and basic shelter.
Your manners are rough cut and badly placed.
You make rubble look organized.
I would measure your sense, but the line comes up short.
A loose stair has better footing than your argument.
You are all weight and no structure.
That remark chipped itself on the way out.
Even dust settles better than you.
I could carve patience into granite before finding yours.
Your confidence is a wall with no mortar.
A crooked corner has more honesty.
You make a pile of rocks look planned.
That thought should be rebuilt from the ground up.
Your words carry weight, but not the useful kind.
You brought heavy talk and no foundation under it.
That kind of weight cracks floors, not arguments.
I have seen broken stonework with better instincts than you.
